summary: This Wikipedia-derived note describes Valencia, Spain: its cultural and architectural development, population and metropolitan area, climate, economy, medieval history of conflict and religious coexistence, and transport. It highlights architects such as Santiago Calatrava and Félix Candela and the City of Arts and Sciences. The note gives conflicting population figures for the city and its metro area, reflecting different sources.
one_line: Overview of Valencia, Spain's third-largest city: its culture, architecture, population, climate, economy, history, and transport links.
key_facts: Valencia is the capital of the autonomous community of Valencia and the third largest city in Spain after Madrid and Barcelona.
The administrative city of Valencia had a population of 809,267 on a land area of 134.6 km2 (52 sq mi).
Valencia's urban area has a population of around 1.5 million people beyond the administrative city limits.
The Port of Valencia is the 5th busiest container port in Europe and the busiest container port on the Mediterranean Sea.
Between 2007 and 2008 there was a 14% increase in the foreign born population of Valencia, with the largest numeric increases from Bolivia, Romania and Italy.
Nearly 84% of Valencia's working population is employed in service sector occupations, while 5.5% work in industry.
The Black Death of 1348 and subsequent epidemics decimated Valencia's population in the mid-fourteenth century.
In 1391 an uncontrolled mob attacked the Jewish quarter of Valencia, causing its virtual disappearance and leading to forced conversion of its surviving members to Christianity.
The Almoravids retook Valencia in 1102 and restored the Muslim religion, and the Almoravid Masdali took possession of the city on 5 May 1109.
The Almohads' entry into Valencia was deterred by Ibn Mardanis, King of Valencia and Murcia until 1171, when the city finally fell to the North Africans.
Valencia has one of the mildest winters in Europe, owing to its southern location on the Mediterranean Sea and the Foehn phenomenon.
Santiago Calatrava produced the City of Arts and Sciences (Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències), which includes an opera house, a science museum, an IMAX cinema/planetarium and an oceanographic park.
Valencia Airport is situated 9 km (5.6 mi) west of Valencia city centre.
The Estació del Nord (North Station) is the main railway terminus in Valencia.
